description: The CLI entry point takes its arguments as a list and returns an exit code; `None` means `sys.argv[1:]`, so tests pass lists and only `raise SystemExit(main())` exits.
What `sys.exit` and `parser.error` raise: a `BaseException`, so `except Exception` does not stop it; it carries the exit code in `.code`.
Called with the raw string; returns the converted value or raises `ArgumentTypeError` (or `ValueError`), which argparse reports as a usage error with code 2.
`add_subparsers(dest=..., required=True)` creates one parser per command; `set_defaults(handler=...)` stores the function to dispatch to.
0 for success, 1 for a runtime failure, 2 for a usage error (argparse's convention).
User text inside a `shell=True` command line can start other commands; pass a list of arguments to `subprocess.run` instead.
